_about: Bracket-notation trees, shared by every implementation that reads them.
The Writer macro (tools/run_macro_test.py) draws each case and checks the
drawing; the JavaScript core (addin/core/tree.js, node --test) parses and
lays each out. 'laid_out' is the macro's own parse and layout of every
case, from TreeLayoutQuiet with the widths recorded beside each node
handed in rather than measured -- so the positions are the macro's
ITEM groups are whole selections for the tree command -- a paradigm of trees -- and 'items_parsed' is the macro's parse of each (ParseLinesQuiet with its tree flag).
arithmetic and not the fonts of the machine that ran it. Written by
LINGUEXX_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 python3 tools/run_macro_test.py; read it before

lines: [{the widest label of all} [A x] [B y]]
wide_parent.why: A parent wider than its children overhangs them on the left, so the layout must shift the whole tree back to x = 0 (LxTMinLeft); no other case does.

comma_after_braces.why: An option after a label's closing brace was read as an empty leaf and a leaf 'roof', and drawn without a word said (seen live, 2026-09-26).

comma_after_leaf.why: The same after a braced leaf: the comma follows a child, not the node's own label.

tab_after_move.why: A tab after 'move' makes it a move line, but the names were cut out with Basic's Trim, which takes spaces only: the macro looked for a node named '<TAB>a' and refused.

too_many_moves.why: ARROW_MAX is 40 and the check is made before a line is kept, so the 42nd line is the one refused.

nbsp_in_brackets.why: The tree reader splits on the same spaces the word splitter does, so a no-break one inside the brackets used to fuse a label to its leaf and produce one node called 'NP him' instead of NP over him.

TREE_REFUSE/trailing_text.error: The tree ends before the selection does; there is still "rubbish" after it.

TREE_REFUSE/not_a_tree.error: A tree has to start with a bracket, like [DP [D the] [NP [N tree]]].

TREE_REFUSE/unknown_option.error: This does not know the node option "align=center".  Only "roof" and "name=..." are supported.

TREE_REFUSE/movement_arrow.error:
This does not read LaTeX (anything with a backslash).

For movement, name the two nodes and put a move line under the tree:
    [CP [DP,name=wh what] [TP [V saw] [DP,name=t __]]]
    move t -> wh

TREE_REFUSE/comma_after_braces.error:
A comma stands on its own after "animaux marins", so what follows it would be drawn as words of the tree.

A node option goes inside the braces, with its label: {animaux marins, roof}.

TREE_REFUSE/comma_after_leaf.error:
A comma stands on its own after "animaux marins", so what follows it would be drawn as words of the tree.

A node option goes inside the braces, with its label: {animaux marins, roof}.

MOVE_REFUSE/no_arrow.error:
A movement line reads "move <from> -> <to>"; this one has no arrow:

    move a b

MOVE_REFUSE/unknown_name.error:
No node is named "zzz".

Name one by adding ", name=zzz" inside its brackets, as in [DP,name=zzz what].

MOVE_REFUSE/self_move.error: A movement line points "a" at itself.

MOVE_REFUSE/moves_only.error: There are movement lines but no tree above them.

MOVE_REFUSE/tikz.error:
This does not read LaTeX (anything with a backslash).

For movement, name the two nodes and put a move line under the tree:
    [CP [DP,name=wh what] [TP [V saw] [DP,name=t __]]]
    move t -> wh

MOVE_REFUSE/too_many_moves.error: That is more movement arrows than this can draw.

ITEM_REFUSE/unclosed.error:
Sub-example a. is not a tree.

A bracket is never closed.

Every item of a numbered tree is a tree.  To put a tree beside a glossed example, make them two examples.
